overview.summary: Sorting algorithms arrange elements in a certain order (usually ascending). Understanding how they work internally is crucial for grasping time complexity limits.
learningObjectives: Understand why O(N^2) sorts (Bubble, Insertion) are too slow for large data.
Understand the mechanics of O(N log N) sorts (Merge Sort, Quick Sort).
Know when to use your language's built-in sort vs writing a custom comparator.
overview.interviewRelevance: While you rarely write a sort from scratch in an interview, you constantly use `.sort()` to enable patterns like Two Pointers or Binary Search.

paragraphs: Imagine having a shuffled deck of 52 cards and trying to find the 7 of Spades. You have to look at every card. But if the deck is sorted, you can find it instantly.
Databases sort their tables. E-commerce sites sort by price. High scores are sorted. Sorting is the most fundamental optimization step before any search.
realWorldHook.ahaMoment: You can't sort anything faster than O(N log N) using comparisons. That is a mathematical ceiling.

definition.technicalDefinition: A Sorting Algorithm puts elements of a list into an order. The most frequently used orders are numerical order and lexicographical order.

vocabulary.definition: The algorithm sorts the array without needing extra memory (e.g., Quick Sort).
Items with the same value retain their original relative order (e.g., Merge Sort).
A custom function passed to a sort method to define how two elements should be compared.

keyProperties: O(N log N) is the fastest comparison-based sort.
O(N) sorting is possible ONLY under strict conditions (e.g., Counting Sort when max value is small).

metaphor: Merge Sort: Divide a giant stack of tests into piles of 1, sort them, then merge pairs of piles together.
Quick Sort: Pick a pivot. Put all tests with lower scores to the left, higher to the right. Repeat on the left and right piles.
mentalModel.clickSentence: Divide and Conquer is the secret to breaking the O(N^2) barrier.

memoryDescription: Merge Sort requires O(N) extra memory to hold the merged arrays.
Quick Sort requires O(log N) extra memory for the recursion stack, but sorts the array in-place.

definitionCode.javascript: arr.sort((a, b) => a - b); // Must provide comparator for numbers!

operations.name: Merge Sort
operations.description: Recursively split the array in half until sizes are 1. Then merge the sorted halves.

code.python:
def mergeSort(arr):
    if len(arr) > 1:
        mid = len(arr)//2
        L = arr[:mid]
        R = arr[mid:]
        mergeSort(L)
        mergeSort(R)
        # Merge logic omitted for brevity

operations.visualNote: Array breaks down to single blocks, then zippers back together.

operations.name: Quick Sort
operations.description: Pick a pivot. Partition array so left < pivot and right > pivot. Recurse on halves.
operations.visualNote: A pivot is selected, and elements swap around it.

patternTemplate.pseudocode:
arr.sort(custom_comparator)
# Now use Binary Search, Two Pointers, or Greedy
patternTemplate.whenToUse: When you need to find duplicates, closest pairs, or optimize an O(N^2) problem down to O(N log N) by organizing the data first.

recognitionQuiz.problemStatement: Given an array of integers, find if any two numbers sum to target. You are not allowed to use extra memory.
recognitionQuiz.explanation: A Hash Map uses O(N) extra memory. If you SORT the array first (in-place, O(N log N) time, O(1) space), you can then use Two Pointers to find the sum.

examples.title: Merge Intervals
examples.problemStatement: Given an array of intervals where intervals[i] = [starti, endi], merge all overlapping intervals.
steps: Sort the intervals based on their start times.
Create an empty result array and push the first interval.
Iterate through the rest of the intervals.
If the current interval's start is <= the last merged interval's end, they overlap! Update the end.
Otherwise, push the current interval to the result.
examples.rationale: By sorting by start time, we guarantee that any overlapping intervals will be directly adjacent to each other in the array.

conceptQuiz.question: In JavaScript, what happens if you call `[10, 2, 30].sort()` without a comparator function?
options: It sorts them alphabetically as strings: [10, 2, 30]
conceptQuiz.explanation: JS `sort()` converts everything to strings by default! '10' comes before '2'. You MUST pass `(a, b) => a - b` to sort numbers correctly.

conceptQuiz.question: What does it mean for a sort to be 'Stable'?
options: If two elements are equal, they remain in the same relative order as they were in the original array.
It always runs in O(N log N) time.
conceptQuiz.explanation: Stability is crucial when you sort by one property (e.g., Last Name), and then sort by another property (e.g., First Name) without messing up the first sort.
